## Best practice: name ports in detail before creating a REC

**Category:** Capella modeling best practice (component ports / REC-RPL)

**The practice:** Before turning a logical component into a Replicable Element Collection (REC), rename its function input/output ports from generic auto-generated labels (`FIP 1`, `FIP 2`, `FOP 1`, ...) to descriptive names that say what each port actually carries and in which direction.

**Why it matters:** A REC gets instantiated multiple times as RPLs. Once you have several replicas, you'll be looking at multiple ports that all say the same generic thing (`FIP 1`, `FOP 1`) on different components, with no way to tell them apart at a glance. Descriptive port names stay self-explanatory regardless of which replica or which side of a connection you're viewing — you don't have to trace back to the exchange or port list to remember what a given port is for. This matters most exactly when it's most tempting to skip: right before replication, when the naming is still cheap to fix and about to get multiplied across every copy.

**Concrete example from this project:** the master station's "Manage States" function and the "Control Machine" functions on its Operator/Line Control actors had these generic ports before renaming:

| Component | Port | Generic name | Descriptive name |
|---|---|---|---|
| Manage States | input | FIP 1 | Operator Commands In |
| Manage States | input | FIP 2 | Line Control In |
| Manage States | output | FOP 1 | Machine Status Out |
| Operator / Control Machine | output | FOP 1 | Operator Commands Out |
| Line Control / Control Machine | input | FIP 1 | Machine Status In |
| Line Control / Control Machine | output | FOP 1 | Line Control Out |

The naming pattern used: **`<what it carries> <In|Out>`** — the direction word makes the port's role unambiguous even out of context, and the "what it carries" half matches the functional exchange name it connects to, so tracing a wire from exchange to port to component is a straight name match rather than a lookup.

**When to apply:** any time a component is a REC candidate, or more generally any component whose ports will be viewed independently of the diagram they were created in (semantic browser, cross-references, another engineer opening just that component). Skip it only for components that will never be replicated and are always viewed with their full diagram context visible.
